idiom_name: typed helper modules registered with the engine (declared ViewHelpers/locals interface)
implementation_notes: The realization is the same registry as in JavaScript (Handlebars.registerHelper, Express app.locals, or the engine's render context), but TypeScript lets the helper contract be declared once: an exported interface for the helpers/locals object types every helper's parameters and return value, and the same object is what the engine receives, so wrong arity or a cents-versus-string mix-up becomes a compile error. In JSX-based server rendering the helper is a typed function returning an element instead of a string. Escaping stays a runtime concern of the engine - the type system cannot see it. The classic helper class collapses into the same exported object of typed functions; a class earns its place only when helpers share mutable configuration, which the engine's registry makes awkward to model anyway.
pitfalls: app.locals is typed as Record<string, any>, so a typo in a template helper name is invisible to the compiler; keep one exported helpers object as the single source of truth.
Handlebars' helper delegate types arguments loosely, so annotate the implementation with the interface - otherwise the helper body silently becomes any.
Minor-unit numbers and formatted strings are both number/string: brand the cents type (or document it) to stop a formatted value being fed back into a helper that expects minor units.
Types vanish at run time: registering helpers through an untyped third-party engine handle still skips the compiler, so keep the registration call next to the typed object.
